name: Cork Dry Gin
production: Compounded gin (Difford's lists it as 'Cold Compounded')
history: 1793 | First distilled at the Watercourse Distillery, Cork
1798 | Recipe transcribed by apprentice distiller William Coldwell
1867 | Cork Distilleries Company formed / bought Watercourse Distillery
1951 | Gladys Leach designs new label with the Cork Coat of Arms
1966 | Cork Distilleries Company merged into Irish Distillers
1988 | Irish Distillers acquired by Pernod Ricard (June)
notes: Best-selling gin brand in Ireland (Wikipedia). Difford's classes it as cold compounded, which conflicts with backlog type 'London Dry Gin' [cần kiểm tra]. Tasting notes from Difford's reviewer (2013).
